source_evidence: Unlike other life insurance, variable life insurance has a cash value that varies depending, in part, on the performance of investments you choose from a menu of investment options—typically mutual funds.
answer: Variable life insurance has a cash value, and its value can rise or fall partly with the performance of the investments you choose. If those investments perform poorly, you could lose money, including some or all of your initial investment. Fees can also reduce the amount of your premium that goes into the account, so the cash value is not guaranteed to grow.
